Disclaimer: the description of the nature and scope of the services and supplies of the Multi-Component Security Monitoring System for the EU Space SOC procurement is only indicative, aimed at outlining the concept in broad terms and it may need substantial adjustments. Therefore, it shall not be considered final nor binding. 
The objective of this procurement procedure is to conclude a Contract for the development, deployment, qualification and support to accreditation of the Multi-Component Security Monitoring System (“MC SECMON”), based on a pre-existing SECMON development baseline, as relevant.
The MC SECMON will contribute to the establishment of the EU Space Security Operations Centre (SOC) enabling the provision of harmonised and state-of-the-art security monitoring capabilities across all components of the Union Space Programme. The Contract may also include optional activities, in particular the maintenance and support to operations of the MC SECMON. The activities to be performed under the Contract include, at high level, the following: 
- Development and integration of the MC SECMON; 
- Deployment and qualification of the MC SECMON; 
- Support to accreditation activities;
- Where the relevant options are exercised, maintenance and support to operations of the MC SECMON; 
- Where the relevant options are exercised, development and deployment of additional MC SECMON enclaves and other system evolutions.

original.description: ERS-EO Proof of Concept on Critical Infrastructure ManagementThe ERS-EO Element 1 Critical Infrastructure Monitoring Prof of Concept is intended to demonstrate the step improvement for enhanced monitoring and management of critical infrastructure resulting from the effective combination of diverse EO and non-EO capabilities representative of the future Earth Observation Governmental Service (EOGS) capacity.  In particular, the customization and fusion of these capabilities will generate significant improvements in tasking response, persistent data collection, information delivery latency, expanded information content andflexibility and adaptability in response to dynamic situations. In this context, the Critical Infrastructure Monitoring PoC will:Stimulate innovative combinations of public and private EO systems to support improved and more flexible tasking, response latency, persistence and cross-operator cueing;Develop customized workflows connecting satellite operators, non-EO data providers, analytics tool developers and critical infrastructure operators to ensure enhanced capability to detect, characterize, respond to and mitigateemergent threats and anomalies;Verify the improvements achievable over current state of the art with respect to emerging threat detection and mitigation action execution for critical infrastructure operators under realistic operating conditions;With respect to gaps in current capabilities, elaborate technical approaches for their resolution, verify their impact under representative operational environments and conditionsand elaborate a road map for eventual transfer to full operations based on exclusively European technology. The contract will integrate existing EO and non-EO capabilities as well as capabilities at an advanced stage of development into a pre-operational network providing a range of analysis support information. The procurement will be structured into three periods as follows:Step[BJ1]  1:requirements consolidation and initial operating capability specification, implementation and testing.Step 2 initial capability demonstrations under realistic operating conditions covering extended routine threat mitigation, timely detection, characterization and response elaboration for emerging threats and anomaly/event response situationsStep 3: extended capability demonstration under fully representative conditions as agreed in the milestone review concluding Step 2 activities All underlying Information and Communication Technology (ICT) functions will be provided by the ERS-EO Element 1 Testbed.

normalized.description: ERS-EO Proof of Concept on Critical Infrastructure ManagementThe ERS-EO Element 1 Critical Infrastructure Monitoring Prof of Concept is intended to demonstrate the step improvement for enhanced monitoring and management of critical infrastructure resulting from the effective combination of diverse EO and non-EO capabilities representative of the future Earth Observation Governmental Service (EOGS) capacity.  In particular, the customization and fusion of these capabilities will generate significant improvements in tasking response, persistent data collection, information delivery latency, expanded information content andflexibility and adaptability in response to dynamic situations. In this context, the Critical Infrastructure Monitoring PoC will:Stimulate innovative combinations of public and private EO systems to support improved and more flexible tasking, response latency, persistence and cross-operator cueing;Develop customized workflows connecting satellite operators, non-EO data providers, analytics tool developers and critical infrastructure operators to ensure enhanced capability to detect, characterize, respond to and mitigateemergent threats and anomalies;Verify the improvements achievable over current state of the art with respect to emerging threat detection and mitigation action execution for critical infrastructure operators under realistic operating conditions;With respect to gaps in current capabilities, elaborate technical approaches for their resolution, verify their impact under representative operational environments and conditionsand elaborate a road map for eventual transfer to full operations based on exclusively European technology. The contract will integrate existing EO and non-EO capabilities as well as capabilities at an advanced stage of development into a pre-operational network providing a range of analysis support information. The procurement will be structured into three periods as follows:Step[BJ1]  1:requirements consolidation and initial operating capability specification, implementation and testing.Step 2 initial capability demonstrations under realistic operating conditions covering extended routine threat mitigation, timely detection, characterization and response elaboration for emerging threats and anomaly/event response situationsStep 3: extended capability demonstration under fully representative conditions as agreed in the milestone review concluding Step 2 activities All underlying Information and Communication Technology (ICT) functions will be provided by the ERS-EO Element 1 Testbed.

original.description: Space Weather Centre for Spain Initial Establishment and Core Capability Developments: Part 1This activity will constitute the initial establishment and operation of a Space Weather Centre for affected stakeholders along with underpinning tools, capabilities and procedures required in order to deliver tailored high quality services to end users. Key user groups are expected to include operators of energy transmission systems, satellite operators, the aviation sector, the Ministry of Defence (MoD) and others. The Centre shall operate in close cooperation with ESA's Space weather Service Network with the aim to establish a node that facilitates collaborative actions with network participants while moving progressively towards a structure with a clear operational dimension ableto support the development and delivery of tailored space weather capabilities and services. Particularly the centre will focus on translating complex space weather information from multiple sources into streamlined, actionable information. A colocation of the development and operations teams shall be foreseen with the aim to streamline the R2O process, support team building and to encouragedirect feedback to research, optimising the use of facilities in ESAC.Part 1 shall include: Systematic mapping of end users and establishment of key contact points with users and stakeholders Establishment of a proactive engagement strategy and actions with the identified end users to ensure full understanding of end user needs and operational requirements Development of necessary IT infrastructure, tools and service operation procedures in order to operate the space weather front desk, initially on an 8/5 basis, with on-call support during periods of elevated space weather activity. OoProcedures shall be developed with a view to transitioning into full 24/7 support at the start of a future Part 2 of this activity. Operation of the space weather front desk from KO+3 months for at least 6 months prior to the start of Part 2 handover Development of a space weather dashboard capabilities targeting end users and building on well demonstrated and tested space weather assets, constituting a layer for translating complex technical concepts into an easy-to-use tool for end users. Training for end users including exercises and simulations based on realistic use casesDevelopment of a roadmap for the operational Centre including priority R2O needs and the inclusion of a space weather testbed facility to be used for regional event simulations and training, bringing together stakeholders including end users, operators and domain experts with a focus on optimising the R2O2R pipeline. Support for data and product provision from existing assetsas part of the service provision shall be foreseen where it does not duplicate activities already funded via the Space Safety Programme's pre operational space weather service activities. Operationalisation of certain key models and tools along with their re-deployment within the Centre may be foreseen subject to the necessary licensing agreements with the asset owner. A handover to Part 2of the activity shall be foreseen.
